releases.name: Release 0
releases.goal: adopted baseline: everything shipped under scaffold-dev through 49f229a (sprints 1.1-1.3, the last closed at 2/4 slices)

releases.name: Release 1
releases.goal: A crypto-futures trader runs the full 10-minute round trip - describe a strategy, watch it compose, backtest it, get one coached change, accept it, re-backtest - inside the PulseTrader desktop app and sees expectancy move, with every step persisted and attributable
real_use_findings: the product has never been used; it is not usable without a UI
exit_criteria: At close, a trader can launch PulseTrader.app from Finder and see every strategy and version persisted in pulse.db in the Strategy Library, with its DSL summary and recent backtest runs — and on a first run with none, an empty state naming the one next action rather than a blank pane.

At close, a trader can describe a strategy in natural language in the Strategy Designer, watch the composer's tool-call steps stream in as they happen, and find the resulting StrategyVersion in the Library.

At close, a trader can select a strategy version in the app, run a backtest, and read expectancy, win rate, equity curve, MFE/MAE, the trade log and the run's provenance header (pair, timeframe, data_version, date range, cost settings) back from the persisted run - a fresh run id, not a cached one.

At close, a trader can ask the coach about a persisted backtest run in the Backtest Lab and get back exactly one validated proposed mutation (it applies to the version's DSL and compiles) with a stated hypothesis - or a recorded failed turn, never silence - then accept, reject or modify it; accepting creates exactly one child StrategyVersion attributed to the coach, re-runs the backtest with the parent run's persisted inputs, and shows expectancy before and after side by side, with the turn's LLM cost and coach-prompt version in the LlmCall ledger. A failure at any step leaves no accepted proposal without its child and no child without its run or a recorded failure.

At close, the operator can run describe -> compose -> backtest -> coach -> accept -> re-backtest inside a Finder-launched PulseTrader.app in under 10 minutes wall-clock, timed from the first keystroke in the Designer, starting from the seeded fixture (a fetched BTCUSDT M15+H4 snapshot at a pinned data_version, a migrated empty pulse.db, a credential file in the app data dir); the expectancy assertion is non-directional - the loop must complete and attribute, not improve.

next_sketch.goal: A trader installs a signed, notarized PulseTrader.app, provisions their LLM credential in Settings (Keychain), and iterates a strategy toward a stated R:R / win-rate target
candidates: Iterate the compose-backtest-coach loop to a target

pending_amendments.reason: audit fold-in: a UI build is a work-item gate and a CI concern, not a product statement that must remain true. It ran dependency installation inside a cumulative suite re-run at every future spine close, putting registry latency into a 600s budget forever. fakes.reason: The real path is 'pulse setup-keys' plus code-signing, so the binary has a stable keychain identity that can read back what it wrote; that is the notarized-build work sketched for the next release. Until someone other than the operator installs the app, a credential file in the app data dir provisions the key at the same cost with none of the signing work, and the release's own exit criterion names that file as part of the fixture rather than claiming provisioning works.
fakes.replacement_trigger: the first person other than the operator installs the app
fakes.status_reason: The product genuinely goes without in-app provisioning. The real path is 'pulse setup-keys' plus code-signing, so the binary has a stable code identity that can read back what it wrote; that is the notarized-build work sketched for r2. The stand-in is a credential file in the app data dir, and its security semantics are WEAKER than the Keychain replacement, not equal: plaintext, readable by any process running as this user, manually provisioned, no code-identity ACL. That delta is the reason this is 'deferred' and not 'real', and r1.s1.w2 bounds it by validating the file fail-closed (refuse it unless it is owner-only, mode 0600, and owned by the running user) so the weakening is enforced rather than assumed. Corrected 2026-08-24 after the spine-plan audit rejected the original 'at the same cost' claim as false.

payload.reason: audit fold-in: a UI build is a work-item gate and a CI concern, not a product statement that must remain true. It ran dependency installation inside a cumulative suite re-run at every future spine close, putting registry latency into a 600s budget forever. Re-homed as an acceptance criterion on r1.s1.w5, where it fails before merge instead of after every future one.

The product genuinely goes without in-app provisioning. The real path is 'pulse setup-keys' plus code-signing, so the binary has a stable code identity that can read back what it wrote; that is the notarized-build work sketched for r2. The stand-in is a credential file in the app data dir, and its security semantics are WEAKER than the Keychain replacement, not equal: plaintext, readable by any process running as this user, manually provisioned, no code-identity ACL. That delta is the reason this is 'deferred' and not 'real', and r1.s1.w2 bounds it by validating the file fail-closed (refuse it unless it is owner-only, mode 0600, and owned by the running user) so the weakening is enforced rather than assumed. Corrected 2026-08-24 after the spine-plan audit rejected the original 'at the same cost' claim as false.

escalation resolved (operator ruling, 2026-08-24): ATTACH the LLM credential handling and redaction gate's controls to r1.s2 as required work — audit trail, least privilege, no-secret-in-log. The coach opens a new LLM path that ships strategy text and backtest numbers to an external model and persists the response, which is the path the gate exists for. Class already bone; this records the ruling and the controls.

internal-enabler admitted: consumed by r1.s4 (r1) — grill gate 2026-08-25 (G2/G3). r1.s2's journey was 'pulse coach <run-id>'; the operator ruled the CLI is a developer/debug surface that carries no user journey, so this spine has none and is an internal-enabler by rung 1. Admitted because r1.s4 (the coach rail) consumes it and is committed in this same release. Consequences: auto: demo lines ONLY, no user: line, and it may not claim product value in any exit criterion. Structural class stays bone (it creates ADR-0021 and hits the money-math risk gate). NOTE: the spine's NAME lacks the '[internal]' marker class-declaration.md §5 asks for, because ossify ships no spine-rename verb; this reason string and RELEASE.md are the durable carriers.

exit_criteria: At close, a trader can launch PulseTrader.app from Finder and see every strategy and version persisted in pulse.db in the Strategy Library, with its DSL summary and recent backtest runs — and on a first run with none, an empty state naming the one next action rather than a blank pane.

At close, a trader can describe a strategy in natural language in the Strategy Designer, watch the composer's tool-call steps stream in as they happen, and find the resulting StrategyVersion in the Library.

At close, a trader can select a strategy version in the app, run a backtest, and read expectancy, win rate, equity curve, MFE/MAE, the trade log and the run's provenance header (pair, timeframe, data_version, date range, cost settings) back from the persisted run - a fresh run id, not a cached one.

At close, a trader can ask the coach about a persisted backtest run in the Backtest Lab and get back exactly one validated proposed mutation (it applies to the version's DSL and compiles) with a stated hypothesis - or a recorded failed turn, never silence - then accept, reject or modify it; accepting creates exactly one child StrategyVersion attributed to the coach, re-runs the backtest with the parent run's persisted inputs, and shows expectancy before and after side by side, with the turn's LLM cost and coach-prompt version in the LlmCall ledger. A failure at any step leaves no accepted proposal without its child and no child without its run or a recorded failure.

At close, the operator can run describe -> compose -> backtest -> coach -> accept -> re-backtest inside a Finder-launched PulseTrader.app in under 10 minutes wall-clock, timed from the first keystroke in the Designer, starting from the seeded fixture (a fetched BTCUSDT M15+H4 snapshot at a pinned data_version, a migrated empty pulse.db, a credential file in the app data dir); the expectancy assertion is non-directional - the loop must complete and attribute, not improve.

payload.name: Toolchain and specta bump: retire the pinned-1.92 workarounds

payload.reason: internal-enabler admitted: consumed by r1.s1 round 2 (r1). This spine has NO user journey — a toolchain bump is not something a user does — so it is an internal-enabler by rung 1, the same disposition as r1.s2 under the 2026-08-25 CLI/dev-surface ruling. Admitted because r1.s1's rounds 2-3 (w5 design-system port, w3 Library, w4 Designer) are committed in this same release and are cheaper to write once against the bumped toolchain than to re-lint afterwards. Consequences: auto: demo lines ONLY, no user: line, and it may not claim product value in any exit criterion. Structural class is bone and NOT a judgment call: oss touch_check over the actual file set returns rc 0 against six registered bones — ADR-0009 (binance/client.rs), ADR-0011 (Cargo.toml, deny.toml), ADR-0012 (agent/composer.rs), ADR-0015 (Cargo.toml, build.rs, src/tauri/**), ADR-0019 (rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, deny.toml), ADR-0020 (src/tauri/**, ui/**). Owes an ADR: the toolchain pin feeds engine_fingerprint, and rust-toolchain.toml's own comment requires a recorded decision to move it.
